changes: Forward destination discovery includes existing group conversations and loads them through the current group store if not initialized. Group discovery failure uses the recoverable destination-load warning rather than a fabricated empty success.

Selected groups refresh membership after attachment materialization, then load existing durable pending work before using groupDMStore.send. Decrypted original File objects and attributed plaintext enter the existing group encryption/send path; source ciphertext is not reused as a destination message.

Groups with unresolved sends are disabled. An uncertain new group operation stays visible with a result-check warning and no success/automatic retry. Confirmed partial delivery or pending local bookkeeping produces a warning directing the user to the group's existing recovery UI, not an unconditional full-success toast.
verification: Five new component regressions cover forwarding through the existing group sender, refreshed membership removal, disabled pending targets/partial result warning, failed group discovery followed by explicit retry, and uncertain operation retention without claiming delivery.

Component group encryption/send functions are mocked; these tests prove destination orchestration, not actual two-client re-encryption. Existing real group-store/storage suites remain in the full regression run.

Initial focused component/locale suites passed: 2 files / 43 tests before the last two regressions were added. Final tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed. Full client suite passed: 229 files / 2205 tests in 46.26s. Vite web production build passed in 717ms. Targeted git diff --check passed; existing warning categories remain visible.
remaining: Source group-message actions still need integration with the shared forwarding surface; this step adds groups as destinations. Richer DM eligibility/block filtering, source revocation races and real two-client re-encryption/attachment delivery remain open.

Crypto initialization, membership epochs, restore scope and pending-send gates remain enforced by the existing group store. No workaround bypasses them; unavailable initialization can still prevent forwarding and needs real-user acceptance.
Overall P0-P11 remains incomplete. No server migration, commit, push, merge, Windows packaging or production release performed.
